ETH-100.q: If correcting false evidence would reveal client confidences, the LLP:

opts.B: Must still take reasonable remedial measures, as candor to the tribunal can override confidentiality

ETH-089.q: Under LLP RPC 3.4, an LLP must not:

opts.B: Unlawfully obstruct access to or alter, destroy, or conceal evidence

ETH-090.q: Falsifying evidence or assisting a witness to testify falsely:

opts.B: Violates the fairness and candor rules
opts.C: Is permitted if it helps the client

ETH-091.q: Knowingly disobeying an obligation under the rules of a tribunal:

opts.B: Violates RPC 3.4 unless based on an open, good-faith assertion that no valid obligation exists

ETH-095.q: In pretrial discovery, an LLP must not:

opts.B: Make a frivolous discovery request or fail to make a reasonably diligent effort to comply with a proper request

ETH-099.q: Requesting a third party (other than a client's relative or agent) to refrain from voluntarily giving relevant information to another party is:

opts.B: Generally prohibited unless the person is a relative/employee/agent and their interests won't be harmed

ETH-092.q: During trial, an LLP must not:

opts.B: Allude to irrelevant or unsupported matters or assert personal knowledge of facts in issue (except when testifying)

ETH-094.q: Improperly influencing a judge, juror, or court official is:

opts.B: Prohibited; an LLP must not seek to influence them by means prohibited by law

ETH-096.q: Meritorious claims and contentions (RPC 3.1) require that:

opts.B: There be a non-frivolous basis in law and fact for the positions asserted

ETH-097.q: Expediting litigation (RPC 3.2) requires the LLP to:

opts.B: Make reasonable efforts to expedite litigation consistent with the client's interests

ETH-101.q: Under LLP RPC 7.1, an LLP must not:

opts.B: Make a false or misleading communication about the LLP or the LLP's services
Identify that the LLP holds a limited license

ETH-109.q: Claiming to be a specialist or 'certified' when not:

opts.B: May be misleading unless the certification is from an approved organization and disclosed properly
Include the words 'Licensed Legal Paraprofessional(s)' in the firm name

ETH-104.q: A solo LLP whose firm name suggests multiple practitioners:

opts.B: May need to clarify, to avoid misleading the public about the number of practitioners

ETH-105.q: The exact words 'Licensed Legal Paraprofessional(s)' must appear:

opts.A: In the firm's URL and email
opts.B: In the business/firm name, though not necessarily within the URL or email address

ETH-106.q: In all court filings, an LLP must:

opts.B: Use the LLP designation to identify themselves as a licensed legal paraprofessional

ETH-107.q: How can the public distinguish an LLP's registration number from an attorney's?

opts.B: LLPs have six-digit numbers beginning with 6; attorneys have five-digit numbers

ETH-108.q: Live, in-person solicitation of a prospective client for pecuniary gain is:

opts.B: Generally restricted, similar to the attorney solicitation rules

ETH-110.q: For an LLP, practicing beyond the authorized scope constitutes:

opts.B: Unauthorized practice and professional misconduct

ETH-111.q: An LLP may assist on an out-of-scope matter only:

opts.B: Under the supervision of a licensed attorney

ETH-112.q: An LLP who employs non-licensed assistants must:

opts.B: Make reasonable efforts to ensure their conduct is compatible with the LLP's professional obligations

ETH-113.q: LLPs are subject to discipline through:

opts.B: The Office of Attorney Regulation Counsel using the attorney discipline and disability procedures

ETH-114.q: Sanctions for LLP misconduct can include:

opts.B: A range up to suspension or disbarment/revocation, depending on severity
opts.C: A fine paid to the client only

opts.B: Engaging in dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation

ETH-117.q: Committing a crime involving dishonesty (e.g., theft, fraud):

opts.B: Can be a basis for discipline as reflecting adversely on fitness

ETH-116.q: If an LLP knows another practitioner committed a serious rules violation raising a substantial question about honesty or fitness, the LLP:

opts.B: May have a duty to report to the appropriate authority

ETH-118.q: Making a false statement on an LLP application or registration is:

opts.B: Misconduct and grounds for denial or discipline

ETH-119.q: To maintain licensure, an LLP must:

opts.B: Complete annual registration and applicable continuing legal education, or face administrative suspension

ETH-120.q: An LLP must not share legal fees with a nonlicensed person or let a nonlicensed person:

opts.B: Own or control the LLP practice or direct professional judgment, except as the rules permit
Publicly disclose whether they carry it, as part of annual registration (it is not currently mandated)

ETH-122.q: An LLP must withdraw from a representation when:

opts.B: Continuing would violate the rules or law, or the LLP's condition materially impairs the representation
opts.C: Fees are unpaid for a day

opts.B: Take steps to protect the client, including notice, returning the file/property, and refunding unearned fees

ETH-124.q: Holding oneself out as able to handle a matter clearly outside LLP scope (e.g., a criminal defense) is:

opts.B: A misleading communication and potential unauthorized practice

ETH-125.q: The recurring ethical theme unique to LLP practice is:

opts.B: Accurately disclosing the limited license and advising clients of scope limits

ETH-126.q: An LLP discovers mid-hearing that a discrete trust-valuation issue (a carve-out) has become central. The LLP should:

opts.B: Advise the client to obtain an attorney for that issue and continue on in-scope matters
opts.C: Withdraw entirely and keep the fee
opts.D: Ask the judge to ignore it

ETH-127.q: Both spouses, who are amicable, ask one LLP to prepare and file their uncontested divorce and split the fee. The LLP should:

opts.A: Represent both to save them money
opts.B: Represent at most one (with disclosure) or neither, because joint representation of opposing parties in the same litigation is barred
opts.C: Represent both with a written waiver

ETH-128.q: An LLP receives a $3,000 advance fee. The proper handling is to:

opts.A: Deposit it in the operating account and spend it
opts.B: Deposit it in the trust account and withdraw amounts only as earned
opts.C: Treat it as a nonrefundable gift

ETH-129.q: During a hearing, the LLP's client testifies to something the LLP knows is false and material. The LLP must:

opts.B: Take reasonable remedial measures, including disclosure to the court if necessary
opts.C: Withdraw silently and keep the secret

ETH-130.q: An LLP's website states 'Smith Family Law' with no indication of license type. This is:

opts.B: Potentially misleading; an LLP-only firm must include 'Licensed Legal Paraprofessional(s)' in the name and disclose the limited license

ETH-131.q: A client asks the LLP to register an out-of-state custody order and pursue punitive contempt. Both requests are:

opts.B: Outside scope (carve-outs); the LLP should refer them to an attorney while assisting with in-scope matters

ETH-132.q: An LLP wants to enter a business deal buying property from a client. The LLP must:

opts.B: Ensure fair terms fully disclosed in writing, advise the client in writing to seek independent counsel, and obtain informed written consent

ETH-133.q: An LLP suspects a paralegal in the office is signing the LLP's name to pleadings without review. The LLP must:

opts.B: Supervise to ensure the assistant's conduct complies with the rules and stop the unauthorized conduct

ETH-134.q: A client demands the LLP pursue a frivolous motion to harass the other parent. The LLP should:

opts.B: Decline, because RPC 3.1 prohibits frivolous filings and the good-faith requirement applies to LLPs

ETH-135.q: The unifying duty an LLP owes when any out-of-scope or competence limit appears is to:

opts.B: Advise the client of the limitation and the need for an attorney, and act within authorized scope
opts.D: Refer the entire case out always
